html:
Nanrantsouak, better known as Norridgewock, was the main village of the Kennebec band of the Abenaki, on the Kennebec River in what is now Maine. The name also stands for the people of the upper Kennebec valley.

The Abenaki here fished for salmon and eels at the river falls, farmed maize and hunted. They belonged to the wider Wabanaki world with the Penobscot and the Arosaguntacook. From the 1690s the French Jesuit Sébastien Rale lived at the village, and it became a base of resistance to English settlement, backed by New France.

In 1724, during Dummer's War, a Massachusetts force attacked Norridgewock, killed Rale and many villagers, and burned the village. Survivors moved to Penobscot country or to the mission villages of Quebec. See also Abenaki.
sum: Nanrantsouak, better known as Norridgewock, was the main village of the Kennebec band of the Abenaki, on the Kennebec River in what is now Maine. The name also stands for the people of the upper Kennebec valley.
